vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: intelligence-suite
Version: 1.0.3

The OpenClaw skill 'intelligence-suite' is classified as benign. The `SKILL.md` clearly outlines its purpose of AI and global news monitoring, specifying required network permissions (openai.com, microsoft.com, firebaseio.com, reuters.com, scmp.com, rthk.hk) and filesystem read access. The Node.js scripts (`scripts/monitor.js`, `scripts/scan.js`) use standard web scraping libraries (axios, cheerio, rss-parser) to fetch and parse news content from the declared sources. There is no evidence of data exfiltration beyond the stated purpose, malicious execution (e.g., `eval`, `child_process`), persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts against the agent. The code is transparent, and dependencies in `package.json` are legitimate and directly used.

llm.summary: The skill is a mostly coherent news scraper, but it can follow untrusted article links outside its declared network scope and feed scraped text back to the agent.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares specific public network domains, but runtime behavior can request linked article URLs and follow redirects without scheme, host, port, or private-address validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a standard npm install, but dependencies use caret ranges and no lockfile is present, so the installed dependency graph is not fixed to the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Scraped webpage text and titles are printed as content for the main agent to synthesize without a clear instruction/data boundary, so hostile article text could influence the resulting briefing if the consuming agent is not careful.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no persistence, scheduled tasks, shell execution, credential access, or local secret reads in the artifact; the main privilege concern is outbound network reach plus npm dependency execution during install.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated AI and global news briefing purpose is broadly matched by RSS/API collection and article scraping, but Hacker News article URLs and feed links can point to arbitrary hosts, which goes beyond the declared source list; the global monitor also adds an entertainment placeholder outside the geopolitics/news purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only in an environment with restricted network egress, because linked articles can cause requests to hosts outside the listed news sources. Treat generated content as untrusted source material, pin dependencies with a lockfile, and avoid giving the consuming agent secrets or high-impact tools while summarizing scraped pages.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed in artifact code: article links from RSS and Hacker News are fetched with axios without destination validation, allowing requests beyond the documented network scope and potential internal-resource exposure through printed snippets.
[T01] expected: Confirmed as a known risk for this design: the skill intentionally summarizes scraped content, but it does not isolate untrusted article text from agent instructions.
[T08] unexpected: Confirmed: package.json uses ranged npm dependencies and the artifact has no lockfile, creating a reproducibility and supply-chain hardening gap rather than evidence of malicious packages.
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted: the core news-monitoring purpose is real, but the implementation is narrower than advertised and includes a hardcoded entertainment/Weibo placeholder that is not clearly disclosed as part of the strategic news purpose.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded after inspection: scripts/scan.js was locally present and fully readable during this review, so the earlier partial-inspection signal is not a current artifact concern.
[SC1] unexpected: Confirmed for axios and rss-parser version ranges; this is a low-level install integrity concern, not direct evidence of hostile behavior.
[SC4] unexpected: Accepted as a dependency-verification concern only: the reviewed manifest does not pin axios, so advisory status cannot be determined from the artifact alone.
